neighbours.label: A noun naming a person's appointed office or candidacy (vice presidential pick, nominee, prelate, titular bishop), vs the same words in non-office senses
fire: Pundits named the governor as the frontrunner for running-mate pick.
He became the party's nominee for the Senate after a close primary.
The pope appointed him titular archbishop of an ancient see.
As a senior prelate, he spoke for the bishops at the council.
She was the president's pick to lead the central bank.
The committee confirmed the nominee for ambassador on Tuesday.
Rumors said the general was the likely vice-presidential pick.
The diocese welcomed the new prelate with a formal mass.
quiet: Pundits said the governor gave a strong speech on farm policy.
He won the primary after a long and expensive campaign.
The titular hero of the film is a lonely detective.
As a senior engineer, he spoke for the team at the review.
She picked a ripe pear from the tree in the garden.
The committee met for lunch on Tuesday after the vote.
Rumors said the general was planning to retire soon.
The diocese repaired the roof of the old cathedral.

predictions: Office/candidacy nouns 0.4-0.9; 'picked a peach', 'titular character', plain senator sentences under 0.1.
